paragraphs: Friend, here's what I think this one is about. Martha does something good: she welcomes Jesus into her home (Luke 10:38). But the text says she was "distracted by all the preparations to be made" (Luke 10:40). A good thing can still pull your eyes off the Guest, and I know that feeling, because I've been that stamper with a hundred cookies to press and no time to look up.

Then Jesus says, "Martha, Martha, you are worried and upset about many things. But only one thing is necessary." (Luke 10:41-42) He doesn't tell her the work is worthless, and I'm not going to say He does. He names what's necessary, and Mary has found it, sitting at His feet and listening (Luke 10:39). I think that's the whole lesson, baker: before you do anything FOR Him, make room to be WITH Him and hear Him.

And look at the promise tucked in the last line: Mary has chosen the good portion, "and it will not be taken away from her." (Luke 10:42) Your to-do list can get interrupted, rearranged, or buried under a pile of dishes, but time spent listening to Jesus is not lost. That's why I keep my ovens ready and my ears open, friend. So today, before the timers start going off, sit down with His Word and let Him talk first.
